Possessing the necessary skills, knowledge, training, and experience

bank.explanation: This is false because excavations should be inspected at the start of every shift, or after any event likely to have affected its stability.

bank.question: Under RIDDOR, an injury must be reported if it results in a worker being unable to perform their normal work duties for more than how many consecutive days?
bank.explanation: Under RIDDOR, any workplace injury that results in an employee being incapacitated for more than 7 consecutive days must be reported within 15 days.

bank.question: Visitors should receive relevant site safety information before accessing work areas
bank.explanation: This is true because visitor controls reduce the chance of exposure to unfamiliar hazards.

bank.question: What does the acronym 'TILE' stand for when performing a manual handling risk assessment?
bank.explanation: Manual handling risk assessments should consider the Task, Individual, Load, and Environment (TILE).

bank.question: Which of the following is true regarding Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS)?
bank.explanation: HAVS (Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome) is permanent and irreversible, though further damage can be prevented by stopping exposure.
options: It is easily cured with medication
It only affects workers over the age of 60
It is a temporary condition that clears up after rest
It is permanent and can cause painful and disabling disorders of the blood vessels, nerves, and joints

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of using 'trench boxes' in an excavation?
bank.explanation: Trench boxes are designed to support the sides of an excavation and prevent them from collapsing on workers, which is the primary risk in deep digging.
options: To prevent people or vehicles falling into the trench
To prevent the sides of the excavation from collapsing
To provide an easy way for workers to climb out of the trench
To keep the bottom of the trench dry from groundwater

bank.question: Under the CDM 2015 Regulations, who is responsible for coordinating health and safety during the pre-construction phase?
bank.explanation: The Principal Designer's primary role under CDM 2015 is to manage H&S during the pre-construction phase and coordinate the design.

bank.question: Regarding site visitors, which of the following statements is true?
bank.explanation: The Principal Contractor is responsible for the health and safety of everyone on site, including visitors, who must be inducted and supervised.
options: They are responsible for their own safety and do not need a site induction
The Principal Contractor is responsible for their safety and site induction
The Client is the only person responsible for visitors
Visitors are not allowed on construction sites under any circumstances

bank.question: What is the industry-standard colour for 110-volt power cables and transformers on a UK construction site?
bank.explanation: The standard color for 110v cables and transformers on UK construction sites is yellow to differentiate it from higher voltages.

bank.question: Under RIDDOR, within how many days must a report be submitted for an injury that results in an employee being away from work for more than seven days?
bank.explanation: RIDDOR 2013 requires accidents resulting in over seven days of incapacitation (not counting the day of the accident) to be reported within 15 days.

bank.question: What is the golden rule for maintaining safety when climbing a ladder?
bank.explanation: While the 1:4 ratio is the angle for a ladder, the 'three-point contact' rule (two hands and one foot, or two feet and one hand) is the primary safety rule for climbing.
options: Always carry tools in your hands while climbing
Maintain three points of contact at all times
Ensure the ladder is at a 60-degree angle
Only use the ladder if you are wearing a safety harness

bank.question: Asbestos must be disturbed to confirm whether it is present
bank.explanation: This is false because suspect asbestos materials should not be disturbed; competent advice and appropriate surveys are needed.

bank.question: Under CDM 2015, who has the primary responsibility for preparing the Construction Phase Plan?
bank.explanation: The Principle Designer is responsible for the Pre-construction Information, while the Principal Contractor must prepare the Construction Phase Plan.

bank.question: Employers are legally required to provide adequate and appropriate first-aid equipment and facilities for all employees on a construction site.
bank.explanation: This is true because according to the Health and Safety (First-Aid) Regulations 1981, employers must provide adequate and appropriate equipment, facilities, and personnel to ensure employees receive immediate attention if they are injured or taken ill at work.

bank.question: Inhaling Respirable Crystalline Silica (RCS) dust can lead to the development of silicosis, a progressive and irreversible lung disease.
bank.explanation: This is true because silica dust is the second biggest killer of construction workers after asbestos, causing serious lung diseases like silicosis and lung cancer.

bank.question: When planning work at height, personal fall protection (such as a safety harness) is the first priority in the hierarchy of control.
bank.explanation: This is false because the hierarchy of control for working at height prioritises avoiding work at height altogether, then preventing falls (e.g., guardrails) before using PPE (e.g., harnesses) to minimize consequences.

bank.question: Site Waste Management Plans (SWMPs) are currently no longer a legal requirement for construction projects in England.
bank.explanation: This is true because site Waste Management Plans (SWMP) are no longer a legal requirement in England, though many contractors still use them as best practice.

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'Toolbox Talk' on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Toolbox talks are short, focused safety briefings intended to refresh knowledge and highlight specific risks relevant to the current day's work.
options: To provide legal training for the Site Manager
To provide short, frequent safety briefings to the workforce on specific topics
To replace the need for a full site induction for new starters
To negotiate pay rates and working hours with subcontractors

bank.question: A supervisor should verify that workers understand a briefing, not merely that they attended it
bank.explanation: This is true because communication is effective only when the workforce understands what is required.

bank.question: What is the four-step management model recommended by the HSE in HSG65 for health and safety management?
bank.explanation: The 'Plan, Do, Check, Act' cycle is the HSE's recommended approach for managing health and safety effectively.

bank.question: Under CDM 2015, who is responsible for managing health and safety risks during the design phase of a project?
bank.explanation: The principal designer is responsible for ensuring health and safety concerns are addressed during the design phase of a project.

bank.question: Environmental controls can include spill prevention and correct waste segregation
bank.explanation: This is true because construction activities must control pollution risks and manage waste responsibly.

bank.question: An HSE inspector can issue a Prohibition Notice in which of the following circumstances?
bank.explanation: A Prohibition Notice is used by the HSE when an inspector believes there is a risk of serious personal injury, stopping the activity immediately.
options: When there is a minor paperwork error in the site files
When the inspector wants to suggest a more efficient way of working
When an activity involves a risk of serious personal injury
When the construction project has exceeded its deadline

bank.question: Towers used in construction where a person could fall two metres or more need suitable inspection records
bank.explanation: This is true because inspection records are required following assembly and at specified intervals for such tower use.

bank.question: Hand-arm vibration exposure should be managed by controlling trigger time and maintaining tools
bank.explanation: This is true because reduced exposure and well-maintained low-vibration tools help prevent HAVS.

bank.question: What is the main purpose of a Method Statement in construction?
bank.explanation: The primary purpose of a Method Statement is to describe exactly how a specific task will be carried out safely, following the risk assessment.
options: To track the cost of materials used on site
To record the daily attendance of the workforce
To list the qualifications of all site managers
To describe the safe system of work for a specific task

bank.question: What is the standard shape and colour for a 'Mandatory' safety sign, such as 'Hard Hats Must Be Worn'?
bank.explanation: Health and safety stickers on construction sites are blue and circular to indicate a mandatory requirement, such as wearing PPE.
options: Blue circle with a white symbol
Yellow triangle with a black border
Red circle with a diagonal bar
Green square with a white symbol

bank.question: The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 explicitly state that all portable electrical tools must be PAT tested every three months.
bank.explanation: This is false because the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 require systems to be maintained to prevent danger; whilst PAT testing is common practice, the regulations focus on the outcome of safety.

bank.question: In manual handling risk assessments, what does the acronym 'TILE' stand for?
bank.explanation: A manual handling assessment should consider the Task, Individual, Load, and Environment (TILE) to identify risks.

bank.question: What is the main purpose of the 'General Principles of Prevention' found within the CDM 2015 Regulations?
bank.explanation: The 'General Principles of Prevention' provide a systematic approach to managing risks by eliminating or reducing them at the source.
options: To provide a list of PPE required for every task
To provide a framework for identifying and managing health and safety risks
To outline the fines associated with health and safety breaches
To provide a template for the Construction Phase Plan

bank.question: Under CDM 2015, who has the primary responsibility for ensuring that 'Pre-Construction Information' is provided to every designer and contractor?
bank.explanation: The Pre-Construction Information is prepared by the Client (with help from the Principal Designer) and provides essential safety data to bidders.

bank.question: Mental health and fatigue can affect safety decisions on site
bank.explanation: This is true because tired or distressed workers may be more likely to make errors or miss hazards.

bank.question: Temporary lighting should be suitable for the work and routes being used
bank.explanation: This is true because poor lighting increases risks from slips, trips, vehicle movements and poor task control.

bank.question: Under the CDM Regulations 2015, who has the legal duty to appoint the Principal Designer and Principal Contractor?
bank.explanation: Under CDM 2015, the Client has the legal responsibility to appoint both a Principal Designer and a Principal Contractor in writing.

bank.question: How do the Work at Height Regulations 2005 define 'work at height'?
bank.explanation: The Work at Height Regulations 2005 state that work at height is any place where, if precautions were not taken, a person could fall a distance liable to cause personal injury.
options: Any place where a person could fall and injure themselves
Only work conducted above 2 metres in height
Work conducted using a ladder only
Work that occurs below ground level in a trench

bank.question: What are 'Toolbox Talks' in the context of site safety communication?
bank.explanation: Toolbox talks are short briefings delivered to the workforce to refresh knowledge on specific site hazards and safety procedures.
options: A formal meeting with a legal solicitor
Short, regular safety briefings for site workers
A yearly training course for senior directors
An interview held after a serious accident

bank.question: What common health condition can be caused by prolonged skin contact with wet cement?
bank.explanation: Dermatitis is a skin condition caused by contact with irritants like wet cement, which is highly alkaline and abrasive.

bank.question: Work at height should be planned and supervised by competent people
bank.explanation: This is true because the Work at Height Regulations require suitable planning, supervision and competence.

bank.question: Which document must all persons on a construction site follow regardless of their specific role or employer?
bank.explanation: The 'Site Rules' are specific to the individual workplace and must be followed by everyone visiting or working on that site.
options: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974
The Site Rules for that specific project

bank.question: A change in weather can require a review of work at height or lifting plans
bank.explanation: This is true because wind, rain and poor visibility can make planned controls unsuitable.

bank.question: According to the Work at Height Regulations, personal protective measures like safety harnesses should always be used in preference to collective measures like guardrails.
bank.explanation: This is false because the hierarchy of control states that collective measures (like birdcage scaffolding) must take priority over personal measures (like harnesses).

bank.question: Under Section 2 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, who has the primary duty to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of all employees?
bank.explanation: Section 2 covers the duties of employers to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of their employees.

bank.question: When installing trench support, how far above the top of the excavation should the support system extend to prevent materials falling in?
bank.explanation: Trench supports should always extend at least 150mm above the top of the excavation to prevent loose material from falling in.
options: At least 150mm above the ground surface
At least 1 metre above the ground surface

bank.question: Which of the following describes the main purpose of health surveillance on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Occupational health monitoring focuses on long-term health risks like respiratory disease or hearing loss, rather than immediate injury.
options: Checking if fire extinguishers are in the correct locations
Ensuring all workers are wearing their hard hats correctly
Identifying early signs of work-related ill health in employees
Counting the number of first aiders available on site

bank.question: Under RIDDOR, certain occupational diseases must be reported to the HSE if a doctor provides written diagnosis that the disease is linked to work.
bank.explanation: This is true because the HSE must be notified within 10 days of the diagnosis of certain occupational diseases, such as carpal tunnel syndrome or occupational asthma.

bank.question: What does the acronym PUWER stand for?
bank.explanation: The main goal of the PUWER regulations is to ensure that work equipment is safe for use, maintained, and inspected.
options: The Personal Use of Work Equipment Regulations
Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations
Primary Utility of Work Equipment Regulations

bank.question: When must an employer consult with their employees on health and safety matters?
bank.explanation: The Health and Safety (Consultation with Employees) Regulations 1996 require employers to consult for the health and safety of staff not covered by a union.
options: Only when a serious accident has already occurred
In good time on matters relating to their health and safety at work
Only if the project lasts longer than 12 months
Once every three years during the annual general meeting

bank.question: Fragile roofs can be treated as safe if they look clean and dry
bank.explanation: This is false because fragile materials may fail without warning and must be protected by suitable controls.

bank.question: The Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 only apply to projects lasting more than 30 working days.
bank.explanation: This is false because the CDM 2015 regulations apply to all construction projects in Great Britain, regardless of their size or length.

bank.question: An HSE inspector issues an 'Improvement Notice' when they believe a person is contravening one or more statutory provisions.
bank.explanation: This is true because an Improvement Notice requires the recipient to remedy a breach of the law within a specified period of time.

bank.question: Which health condition is a major risk for workers in sewers or those working near contaminated water sources?
bank.explanation: Leptospirosis (Weil's Disease) is often carried in the urine of rats and can enter the body through cuts or the mouth/nose.

bank.question: A scaffold tag alone is not a substitute for a proper inspection regime
bank.explanation: This is true because tags help communicate status, but inspections must still be completed by competent people.

bank.question: What is the maximum period a scaffold used for work can remain in place before it must be re-inspected by a competent person?
bank.explanation: An inspection must be carried out at least every 7 days, or after any event likely to have affected its stability.

bank.question: Under RIDDOR, an over-seven-day injury must be reported within 15 days of the incident. What is the definition of an over-seven-day injury?
bank.explanation: RIDDOR requires a report for any work-related accident that results in an employee being unable to perform their normal work duties for more than seven consecutive days.

bank.question: If a self-employed contractor is seriously injured on your site, it is their personal responsibility, not the site manager's, to report it under RIDDOR.
bank.explanation: This is false because the RIDDOR report must be submitted by the 'responsible person' (usually the employer or site manager), regardless of the victim's employment status.

bank.question: Which notice can an HSE inspector serve that requires an activity to stop immediately until the risk is reduced?
bank.explanation: A prohibition notice is issued when an inspector believes there is a risk of serious personal injury and requires the activity to stop immediately.

bank.question: What category of equipment do dust masks and respirators fall under?
bank.explanation: Dust masks fall under Respiratory Protective Equipment (RPE), which is a specific subset of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
options: COSHH (Control of Substances Hazardous to Health) masks

bank.question: Portable electrical tools should be checked visually before use
bank.explanation: This is true because obvious damage to plugs, leads or casings can indicate a serious electrical risk.

bank.question: Trailing leads should be routed or protected to reduce trip and damage risks
bank.explanation: This is true because cable management helps prevent falls and electrical damage.

bank.question: What does a circular blue safety sign with a white symbol represent?
bank.explanation: Safety signs with a blue circle and white symbol are mandatory signs, meaning a specific action or PPE must be taken.

bank.question: Which of the following would be covered under the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH) Regulations?
bank.explanation: COSHH assessments focus on substances that can harm health, which includes fumes and dust generated by work processes.

bank.question: According to the Work at Height Regulations 2005, when must edge protection be used?
bank.explanation: The Work at Height Regulations require fall protection (such as guardrails) for any work where there is a risk of a fall liable to cause personal injury.
options: At any height where a fall can cause personal injury
Only when working above 2 metres in height
Only when working above 4-to-1 ratio ladder height
When working in an area with a 5% or higher incline

bank.question: What long-term health condition is caused by the regular and frequent use of hand-held power tools like breakers or sanders?
bank.explanation: HAVS is a permanent, painful condition affecting blood vessels and nerves, often caused by prolonged use of vibrating power tools.

bank.question: Materials should be stacked so they are stable and do not obstruct access routes
bank.explanation: This is true because unstable or badly located stacks can fall, block escapes or cause trips.

bank.question: The HSE 'FFI' scheme relates to cost recovery for inspections. What does FFI stand for?
bank.explanation: The FFI scheme allows the HSE to recover costs from businesses that are found to be in material breach of health and safety laws.

bank.question: What does a red square or rectangular safety sign with white lettering or symbols indicate?
bank.explanation: A red square or rectangular sign with white symbols (such as a flame) is used to indicate the location of fire-fighting equipment.
options: Warning of a hazard (e.g., fragile roof)

bank.question: Green signs are commonly used for safe conditions such as first aid or escape routes
bank.explanation: This is true because green safety signs identify emergency escape and first aid information.

bank.question: Under the Work at Height Regulations 2005, what is the maximum height a ladder can be used for work?
bank.explanation: According to the Work at Height Regulations 2005, a risk assessment must be carried out to select the most suitable equipment; there is no specific height 'limit' for using ladders.
options: There is no set height limit if the task is low risk and short duration
Ladders can only be used for access, not for work

bank.question: Under CDM 2015, who has the ultimate responsibility for ensuring a project is set up safely?
bank.explanation: While the Principal Contractor manages the site, the Client is legally responsible for ensuring that the Principal Contractor is competent and has the necessary resources.

bank.question: Under the Working Time Regulations, what is the maximum average weekly working limit for an adult worker who has not opted out?
bank.explanation: The legal maximum weekly working limit under the Working Time Regulations is 48 hours, averaged over 17 weeks, unless an employee 'opts out' in writing.

bank.question: HAVS symptoms can include tingling, numbness and reduced grip strength
bank.explanation: This is true because these symptoms indicate damage to nerves and blood vessels in the hand and fingers.

bank.question: If a member of the public is injured on a construction site and taken directly to a hospital for treatment, the incident is reportable under RIDDOR.
bank.explanation: This is true because under RIDDOR, accidents involving a member of the public must be reported if they are taken from the site directly to a hospital for treatment for that injury.

bank.question: Under CDM 2015, a project is notifiable to the HSE if the construction work is scheduled to last longer than:
bank.explanation: The CDM 2015 regulations require the client to notify the HSE for projects lasting >30 working days with >20 workers at any one time, or exceeding 500 person days.
options: 10 Working days and more than 5 workers
20 Working days and more than 10 workers
30 Working days and more than 20 workers at any one time
60 Working days and more than 50 workers

bank.question: How is Leptospirosis (Weil's Disease) most commonly contracted on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Leptospirosis (Weil's Disease) is a bacterial infection often spread through the urine of infected rats, commonly found in contaminated water or wet ground.
options: Inhaling wood dust without a mask
Working in high-decibel environments without ear defenders
Contact with water or wet ground contaminated by rat urine
Lifting heavy blocks with incorrect posture

bank.question: Site management should monitor controls rather than assuming they remain effective
bank.explanation: This is true because inspection and supervision confirm whether controls are being used and still work.

bank.question: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, who has the primary duty to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of employees?
bank.explanation: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 places the primary duty of care on the employer to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of all employees.

bank.question: What is the primary reason for recording 'near miss' incidents on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Near misses indicate failures in safety systems and provide an opportunity to prevent future injury-causing accidents.
options: To identify trends and prevent more serious accidents in the future
To ensure the health and safety executive (HSE) is informed of all minor incidents
To identify which workers are prone to making mistakes for disciplinary action
To satisfy the requirements of the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR)

bank.question: Which of the following describes the powers of an HSE Inspector regarding site access?
bank.explanation: An HSE Inspector has the legal power to enter any premises at any reasonable time (or anytime if they believe a dangerous situation exists) to carry out an inspection.
options: Only when the site manager has been given 24 hours' notice
Only when accompanied by a police officer
At any reasonable time, or at any time if they believe a dangerous situation exists

bank.question: On a construction site, what does a safety sign with a red circle and a cross-bar on a white background signify?
bank.explanation: Safety signs with a red circle and a diagonal line through a black pictogram indicate a prohibition (something you must not do).

bank.question: What is the primary meaning of a yellow triangular sign with a black border?
bank.explanation: The yellow section of a site safety sign denotes a warning, such as 'Caution' or 'Danger'.
options: A warning of a particular hazard

bank.question: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 is the primary piece of legislation governing occupational health and safety in Great Britain.
bank.explanation: This is true because the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 is the primary piece of legislation that sets out the general duties of employers, employees, and the self-employed in the UK.

bank.question: A banksman should use agreed signals and remain in a safe position
bank.explanation: This is true because clear communication and a safe viewpoint help control vehicle movements without putting the banksman at risk.

bank.question: On many modern construction sites, what does a green or amber flashing beacon on a plant vehicle usually signify?
bank.explanation: The yellow/amber light on a construction vehicle or plant usually indicates that the operator's seatbelt is correctly fastened.
options: The vehicle's engine is running hot
The vehicle is exceeding its safe load limit
The operator has their seatbelt securely fastened

bank.question: A written Health and Safety Policy is only a legal requirement for companies with five or more employees.
bank.explanation: This is false because under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, all employers must have a written policy if they have 5 or more employees, not 10.

bank.question: Alcohol or drugs that impair performance are acceptable if the worker feels capable
bank.explanation: This is false because impairment creates serious safety risks and must be managed through site rules and support.

bank.question: A method statement is essentially a work plan that describes exactly how a specific task will be carried out safely.
bank.explanation: This is true because method statements are often used to expand upon the findings of a risk assessment by providing a chronological, safe sequence of work.

bank.question: Scaffold alterations should be made only by competent people authorised to do so
bank.explanation: This is true because unauthorised changes can weaken the scaffold and create fall risks.

bank.question: Which type of fire extinguisher is generally most suitable for fires involving flammable liquids, such as petrol or oil?
bank.explanation: Fires involving flammable liquids (Class B) should be tackled with Foam or Dry Powder, never water.

bank.question: What is the most effective method for controlling dust when using a cut-off saw on concrete blocks?
bank.explanation: Dust suppression (using water) or local exhaust ventilation (LEV) are the most effective ways to stop silica dust from becoming airborne.
options: Using water suppression or on-tool extraction (LEV)
Giving the worker a standard cloth face mask
Opening all the windows in the room

bank.question: In fire safety, what type of fuel is involved in a 'Class B' fire?
bank.explanation: Class B fires involve flammable liquids like petrol or oil. Foam or Dry Powder are typically used; Water must never be used on Class B fires.
options: Solid materials like wood and paper
Flammable liquids such as petrol or oil
Flammable gases like butane or propane

bank.question: What is the immediate action required if a worker discovers material they suspect contains asbestos during a refurbishment project?
bank.explanation: Asbestos must be identified and managed before work starts; if it is suspected later, work must stop immediately to prevent exposure.
options: Continue working but wear a standard dust mask
Move the material to a designated waste skip immediately
Wet the material down and continue the task
Stop work immediately, evacuate the area, and inform site management

bank.question: Under what circumstances can the HSE issue a 'Fee for Intervention' (FFI) invoice to a company?
bank.explanation: A 'Fee for Intervention' (FFI) is charged by the HSE when an inspector discovers a 'material breach' of health and safety law during a site visit.
options: Whenever an inspector visits a site for any reason
Only when an accident has resulted in a fatality
When the site manager requests a safety audit from the HSE
When an inspector identifies a 'material breach' of the law

bank.question: According to the COSHH hierarchy of control, what is the preferred first option for managing a hazardous substance?
bank.explanation: COSHH requires employers to prioritize safer alternatives before relying on personal protective equipment.
options: Providing high-quality PPE for all workers
Substituting the substance with a less hazardous one
Limiting the time workers are exposed to the substance

bank.question: What is generally considered the 'minimum' PPE required for entry onto a standard UK construction site?
bank.explanation: Safety Boots and High-Visibility vests are standard PPE requirements on almost all UK construction sites to prevent foot injuries and ensure visibility.

bank.question: Which regulations cover the legal requirement to report certain workplace accidents, near misses, and occupational diseases?
bank.explanation: The Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR) 2013 is the primary legislation for reporting workplace accidents.

bank.question: According to the HSE, when is it acceptable to use a ladder as a working platform?
bank.explanation: The Work at Height Regulations 2005 state that work should only be carried out from a ladder when the risk is low and the duration of the task is short (less than 30 minutes).
options: Any duration as long as the ladder is tied off
Short duration (less than 30 minutes) and low risk tasks
Up to two hours if the worker has a harness on
Ladders are now banned for all construction work tasks

bank.question: An HSE inspector can issue a Prohibition Notice even if no specific health and safety regulations have been breached at that moment.
bank.explanation: This is true because the HSE may issue a Prohibition Notice if they believe an activity poses a risk of serious personal injury, even if no law has yet been broken.

bank.question: Under the Display Screen Equipment (DSE) Regulations, what is a legal requirement for 'users' who work on monitors?
bank.explanation: Employers must provide an 'eyesight test' and corrective lenses specifically for VDU work if the test shows they are required.
options: Be offered an eyesight test at the employer's expense
Receive a free pair of designer sunglasses for outdoor site visits
Be limited to 15 minutes of screen use per day maximum
Only work on the ground floor to prevent eye fatigue from stairs

bank.question: In accordance with the Work at Height Regulations 2005, what is the correct hierarchy of control measures?
bank.explanation: The Work at Height Regulations 2005 follow a hierarchy: Avoid work at height if possible, then prevent falls (e.g., guardrails), and finally mitigate the distance and consequences of a fall.

bank.question: Asbestos is considered harmless as long as the material is in good condition and is not being disturbed or broken.
bank.explanation: This is false because asbestos-containing materials (ACMs) are most dangerous when they are damaged or disturbed, as this releases the microscopic fibres into the air.

bank.question: Why is it essential for a site manager to consult with the workforce on health and safety matters?
bank.explanation: Employers have a legal duty to consult with their employees on anything that may substantially affect their health and safety.
options: To save money on insurance premiums
Because it is a legal requirement under the Consultation with Employees Regulations
To ensure the project finishes ahead of schedule
So that workers can be blamed if an accident occurs

bank.question: A construction company with only three employees is legally required to have a written record of their risk assessments under the Management Regulations.
bank.explanation: This is false because under the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, risk assessments must be recorded if the employer has five or more employees.
